clue.text: Dance in a cape before a sort of organ

parts.note: Cape Horn, the southern tip of South America, is a famous cape
a pipe organ is one kind of organ, and a pipe is a sounding part of it

explanation.surface: Someone dances wearing a cape in front of an organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a cape' means a particular named cape, the one at South America's tip; 'before' orders the two pieces, and 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively solo dance traditionally associated with sailors.

clue.text: Here is an invitation by Aunt Sally's manager

definitions.text: an invitation by Aunt Sally's manager
definitions.meaning: the fairground showman invites throwers to strike the dummy, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: Aunt Sally is a British fairground game in which players throw sticks at a wooden figure of a woman; split in two the answer is the showman's cry to strike her.
explanation.definitionFit: An old adverb for to this place; split, it is the cry to strike the figure.

clue.text: A man's address in the bar is a rigid thing

indicators.note: the article and the title go in the bar

parts.note: a rod is a bar
Mr is the way to address a man

explanation.surface: A lawyer's speech in court is stiff and unbending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container. The surface suggests a barrister's address in court; here the bar is just a metal rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod for packing a gun's charge, proverbially stiff and straight.

clue.text: You could write on this portion about church servants

indicators.note: the portion goes about the church and servants

parts.note: a part is a portion
men can mean servants or attendants

explanation.surface: A section of writing material about the staff of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container; 'servants' as men is an old usage, as in men-at-arms or a lord's men.
explanation.definitionFit: Prepared animal skin used as a writing surface.

clue.text: Later quality, or one among those still to come

indicators.note: the two short pieces go among the letters of the word for future generations

parts.note: posterity means future generations
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Whether something is later, or just one of the generations to come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' signals the container; the commas the surface suggests between the pieces are not there, so 'or one' runs straight on.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of coming after something else in time.

clue.text: Couple, right to get a pick-me-up

parts.note: a brace is a pair, as of game birds

explanation.surface: A pair, with permission, get themselves a restorative.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff drink that restores one's spirits is a tonic of this kind.

clue.text: Tirade in which one is smiling

indicators.note: the letter for one goes in the tirade

parts.note: a rant is a tirade
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A tirade during which one person grins.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary word for laughing or cheerful, from French.

clue.text: Italy's Roman heel is now its toe

definitions.text: Italy's Roman heel is now its toe

parts.words: Italy's Roman heel is now its toe
parts.note: the Roman region of this name lay in the heel of Italy, but the modern region of the name is in the toe

explanation.walkthrough: The Romans gave the name to the heel; it later moved to the south-western peninsula.
explanation.definitionFit: A region whose name moved from the heel to the toe of the Italian boot.

clue.text: Apostate about to renounce an opinion all round

indicators.note: the word for renouncing goes all round the word for about

parts.note: to recant is to renounce a belief
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A turncoat is about to abandon his views entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all round' signals the container; the first 'about' is wordplay, not a sign that the apostate is on the point of acting.
explanation.definitionFit: One who deserts a faith or cause.

clue.text: Headgear — a danger with this shrub

parts.note: a tam is a Scottish woollen cap, short for tam-o'-shanter
risk means danger

explanation.surface: Wearing a hat near this bush is somehow hazardous.
explanation.definitionFit: A feathery-leaved bush of salt-tolerant coastal ground.

clue.text: Bitter quality, one with many of the French

parts.note: gall is bitterness, from bile
I is the Roman numeral one
C, the Roman numeral for a hundred, stands for many

explanation.surface: Bitterness is a trait shared by plenty of French people, it suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaul was France's ancient name, so this adjective means belonging to France.

clue.text: Splendid tea a nun mixed to retire

parts.note: super means splendid

indicators.note: mixed signals the letters of tea, a and nun stirred together

explanation.surface: A nun brewing a fine cup of tea before stepping down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges TEA A NUN into ANNUATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To pension off, or step down from work on a pension.

clue.text: Hope to return round about the start of an era

indicators.note: the reversed word goes round the letter for about
returning means the word for hope is read backwards

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to come back around the dawn of a new age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns HOPE into EPOH, and 'round' puts C inside it before the final H.
explanation.definitionFit: Its original sense was the fixed point in time from which a new period is reckoned.

clue.text: Quite wrong — clever — just

indicators.note: wrong signals the word quite set out in a wrong order

parts.note: able means clever or capable

explanation.surface: A string of verdicts: quite wrong, clever, merely adequate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' signals an anagram of the first word only; the dashes make the clue look like a list of verdicts.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair and impartial, as a just settlement is.

clue.text: Careful thought — in slow motion

definitions.meaning: long and careful consideration of a matter
moving with this quality means moving slowly and steadily

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both careful consideration and an unhurried, measured way of moving.

clue.text: Poor Una carrying fruit-for an unintelligent operator

indicators.note: the jumbled name carries the fruit inside it
poor signals the name Una in a poor, jumbled form

parts.note: the tomato is botanically a fruit

explanation.surface: Poor Una lugging fruit for some dim-witted worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' is the anagram signal on the name and 'carrying' the container; the fruit sits between the second and third letters of the jumbled name.
explanation.definitionFit: A robot or a person acting mechanically without thought.

clue.text: Blotted out, outshone

definitions.meaning: hidden from view, as the sun by the moon
surpassed so as to be overshadowed

explanation.definitionFit: Obscured, as by a heavenly body, or overshadowed by a rival.

clue.text: Row about a garment

parts.note: to pull is to row, a pull being a stroke of the oar
over means about, as in talk over

explanation.surface: An argument over a piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel but means rowing a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted top put on over the head; British jumper.

clue.text: Oppose roles as doubles:

parts.note: to counter is to oppose
an actor's roles are parts

explanation.surface: Contrasting roles are played as twins on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact equivalents or matching opposite numbers.

clue.text: Sweet toy

definitions.meaning: a pudding of sponge, custard and cream
to toy with is to dally or play idly

explanation.definitionFit: Both a layered dessert and a verb meaning to play idly.

clue.text: Corners early invaders

definitions.meaning: the meeting points of two lines
a Germanic people who invaded Britain in the fifth century

explanation.definitionFit: Both the geometric meeting points of lines and the tribe that gave England its name.

clue.text: It's about a sweet drink available in part of London

indicators.note: the word it goes about the drink

parts.note: the word it, the 's being only part of the surface
a sling is a sweetened spirit drink, as in gin sling
on means available, as on tap

explanation.surface: A pub guide says a sweet cocktail can be had in one district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container; the 's of It's is surface only. The answer is a borough of north London.
explanation.definitionFit: A borough in north London.

clue.text: Nobody round about for the time being

indicators.note: the word for nobody goes round the letter for about

parts.note: none means nobody
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: There is no one around for now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts C inside NONE; the definition is used in the phrase for the nonce.
explanation.definitionFit: Used in the phrase for the nonce, meaning for the present occasion only.

clue.text: A dimwit to look listlessly around the river

indicators.note: the word for looking listlessly goes around the river letter

parts.note: to moon is to gaze or mope about listlessly
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A dullard gazes vacantly about by the riverside.
explanation.definitionFit: An insulting term for a stupid person.

clue.text: Learned man brooded without brief advantage

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the word for brooded goes around

parts.note: a hen that broods sits on her eggs, so brooded means sat
van is the short form of advantage in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A scholar sulks over having no quick edge over his rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: SAT surrounds VAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar of deep knowledge.

clue.text: Faults we possibly find extravagant

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: The failings we may consider excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Spending or using things lavishly and needlessly.

clue.text: With divine around composer is confounded

indicators.note: the divine's letters go around the composer

parts.note: a DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a divine
Thomas Arne, English composer of Rule, Britannia

explanation.surface: A composer surrounded by clergymen is baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: A divine is a clergyman; DD (Doctor of Divinity) stands for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild euphemism for damned, as in a damned nuisance.

clue.text: Muddle about girl's shabby quality

indicators.note: the word for muddle goes about the girl's name

parts.note: a mess is a muddle
Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Confusion over a young woman's scruffy appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: Shabbiness or poor, mean condition.
